blocking_findings: F1 [Blocker] review-c: scripts/old-browser-check.mjs:130-139,202-232 counts input attempts as moves and treats any change in serialized state as a move. The simulation increments timeMs without input, so the gate can exit 0 when the game ignores every input. Require a player-action state transition and count accepted moves.

F2 [Blocker] review-c: scripts/old-browser-check.mjs:34,226-230 performs output I/O without a cleanup guarantee. If writing check.json throws, it skips browser and server cleanup. Keep cleanup independent of artifact writes and report filesystem failures without a stack.

F3 [Blocker] review-c: scripts/old-browser-check.mjs:95-105 accepts any successful response at the fixed URL before the strict-port child reports exit. An existing demo can answer before the spawned server binds. Verify that the responding server belongs to this run before accepting browser evidence.
nonblocking_findings: F4 [Nit] review-c: scripts/old-browser-check.mjs:26-32 prints the same usage line and exits 1 for both --help and an invalid game. Support explicit help with exit 0 and name the invalid value in the error. The parser also ignores extra arguments if the first --game value is valid.

F5 [Nit] review-c: scripts/old-browser-check.mjs:142,221,225 omits state_changed in failure JSON and inserts stack traces into the errors array that it prints to stdout. Initialize the field to false and emit concise error messages.
